# odinex_server (Resource)

Manages an Odinex Cloud server.

Changing `server_type` powers the server off, changes the type and powers it on again. Changing `image` rebuilds the server (all data on its disk is lost).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "odinex_server" "web" {
  name         = "web-1"
  server_type  = "s2"
  image        = "ubuntu-24.04"
  location     = "fra1"
  ssh_keys     = [odinex_ssh_key.admin.id]
  firewall_ids = [odinex_firewall.ssh.id]
  backups      = true
  labels       = { role = "web" }

  network {
    network_id = odinex_network.private.id
    ip         = "10.0.1.5"
  }

  public_net {
    ipv4_enabled = true
    ipv6_enabled = true
  }
}

# A server without public IPs: it reaches the internet through the network's
# NAT gateway and is reached through an Elastic IP or a load balancer.
resource "odinex_server" "app" {
  name        = "app-1"
  server_type = "s2"
  image       = "ubuntu-24.04"
  location    = "fra1"
  ssh_keys    = [odinex_ssh_key.admin.id]

  network {
    network_id = odinex_network.private.id
  }

  public_net {
    ipv4_enabled = false
    ipv6_enabled = false
  }

  depends_on = [odinex_nat_gateway.private]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `image` (String) Name or ID of the image (e.g. `ubuntu-24.04`, or a snapshot ID). Changing it rebuilds the server.
- `location` (String) Location (region) name, e.g. `fra1`.
- `name` (String) Name of the server (hostname-safe: letters, digits, dots and dashes).
- `server_type` (String) Name or ID of the server type (e.g. `s2`). Can be changed in place: the server is powered off, resized and powered on.

### Optional

- `backups` (Boolean) Enable daily backups (+20 % of the server price). Disabling deletes all existing backups.
- `delete_protection` (Boolean) Prevent the resource from being deleted. Defaults to `false`.
- `firewall_ids` (Set of Number) IDs of firewalls applied directly to the server (at most 5 at creation; they are active before the first boot). Changes apply or remove the firewalls in place. Only tracked while set; firewalls applied through label selectors are not listed. Use either this or `odinex_firewall.apply_to` / `odinex_firewall_attachment` for a given server, not both.
- `keep_disk` (Boolean) When changing `server_type`, keep the current disk size so the server can be downgraded later. Defaults to `false` (the disk is upgraded).
- `labels` (Map of String) User-defined labels (key/value pairs). Up to 64 pairs; keys and values up to 63 characters.
- `network` (Block Set) Private networks to attach the server to. Networks are attached and detached in place. Do not combine with `odinex_server_network` for the same server. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--network))
- `placement_group_id` (Number) ID of the placement group. The API only sets it at creation, so changing it recreates the server.
- `primary_network_id` (Number) Network a server without public IPs (`public_net` with both disabled) lives on: it is attached at creation and the server reaches the internet through its `odinex_nat_gateway`. Defaults to the only `network` block; required when there are several. Its `network` block cannot have a fixed `ip`. Changing it recreates the server.
- `public_net` (Block, Optional) Public network configuration. Changing it recreates the server. Disable both for a server without public IPs: it needs a network (see `primary_network_id`) and is reachable through an `odinex_elastic_ip` or a load balancer with `network_id`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--public_net))
- `shutdown_before_deletion` (Boolean) Gracefully shut the server down before deleting it. Defaults to `false`.
- `ssh_keys` (List of String) SSH key names or IDs to install. Changing them recreates the server. Without SSH keys a root password is generated (not stored).
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `user_data` (String) Cloud-init user data. Changing it recreates the server.

### Read-Only

- `backup_window` (String) UTC hours of the daily backup, e.g. `22-02`; empty when backups are off.
- `id` (String) Unique ID of the resource.
- `ipv4_address` (String) Public IPv4 address (empty when IPv4 is disabled).
- `ipv6_address` (String) Public IPv6 address (empty when IPv6 is disabled).
- `primary_disk_size` (Number) Size of the primary disk in GB.
- `primary_ipv4_id` (Number) ID of the primary IP holding the public IPv4 address (use it with `odinex_rdns.primary_ip_id`).
- `primary_ipv6_id` (Number) ID of the primary IP holding the public IPv6 address.
- `status` (String) Status of the server (`running`, `off`, …).

<a id="nestedblock--network"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network`

Required:

- `network_id` (Number) ID of the network.

Optional:

- `ip` (String) Fixed IP inside the network; assigned automatically when omitted.


<a id="nestedblock--public_net"></a>
### Nested Schema for `public_net`

Optional:

- `ipv4_enabled` (Boolean) Assign a public IPv4 address. Defaults to `true`.
- `ipv6_enabled` (Boolean) Assign a public IPv6 address. Defaults to `true`.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by ID or by name. network/public_net blocks, ssh_keys and user_data are not imported.
terraform import odinex_server.web 42
terraform import odinex_server.web web-1
```
